clue.text: Creating a garden in the west Indies

indicators.note: creating means making something new, so the letters of the words a garden are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is laying out a garden on a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creating' rearranges A GARDEN. The definition is a description of where the place is: an island nation in the West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is a Caribbean island country, one of the Windward Islands of the West Indies.

clue.text: Reforms enraged this aristocrat

indicators.note: reforms means forms again, so the letters of the word enraged are shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A noble is furious at political reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reforms' looks like a noun about politics but is a verb telling you to re-form ENRAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a Spanish or Portuguese nobleman of the highest rank, hence any high-ranking aristocrat.

clue.text: He brought out the earlier model

parts.note: ex- means former or earlier, as in an ex-husband
a model is someone who poses, a poser

explanation.surface: A man introduced a previous version of a product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought out' reads as launching a product but means revealed: an exposer is one who exposes, or brings things out into the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reveals or uncovers a secret is the one who exposes it.

clue.text: A quiet one, but fast!

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Something that is quiet yet speedy, like a stealthy car.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an old-fashioned adverb for swiftly or at speed.

clue.text: A despot in confusion may appear quite the opposite

indicators.note: a muddle or confusion of the letters in the words a despot plus in gives a new order

explanation.surface: A muddled tyrant might seem to be the reverse of what he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of the phrase 'in confusion' but is fodder; 'confusion' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The antipodes are places diametrically opposite on the globe, and figuratively the exact opposite of something.

clue.text: An exacting Shakespearean role

parts.note: exacting reads as demanding, but here means extracting payment: the moneylender in The Merchant of Venice who insists on his pound of flesh

explanation.surface: A demanding part for an actor in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exacting' looks like 'difficult to play'; it really means exacting a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: The usurer of The Merchant of Venice demands a pound of flesh as forfeit for an unpaid loan.

clue.text: Step indoors

parts.note: a step found inside a house, one of a flight leading to the upper floor

explanation.definitionFit: A single tread of a staircase is a step inside a building.

clue.text: The standard set, policemen stand firm

parts.note: the Yard, Scotland Yard, is London's Metropolitan Police headquarters, standing for its officers
to stick is to stay put and not give way

explanation.surface: Officers refuse to budge on agreed standards.
explanation.walkthrough: THE YARD (Scotland Yard) is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police; 'set' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a measure or benchmark against which things are judged.

clue.text: Artistry when at the crease?

parts.note: the crease suggests a cricket batsman's stroke play, but it is a fold in paper made by the Japanese folding art

explanation.surface: A batsman showing skill at the crease in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the line where the batsman stands, so the surface suggests elegant batting; the creases here are folds in paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper-folding is the art of making shapes by creasing sheets.

clue.text: Thieves' child not long in the family

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: kin means one's relatives or family
an inch is a short length, not long

explanation.surface: A young criminal has only recently joined the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not long' looks like 'recently', but it means a short measure. Thieves' cant is the old slang of criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: In old thieves' cant the word was slang for a young child.

clue.text: Stop after snake is seen on the road

indicators.note: after says the word for stop comes behind the snake

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
to halt is to stop

explanation.surface: A driver halts after a snake is spotted on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac road surfaces are made of bitumen mixed with gravel.

clue.text: Charge that's sound as a rule

indicators.note: sound tells you the words are heard rather than spelled

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule

explanation.surface: An accusation that seems reasonable and principled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'valid' but signals a homophone: A REIGN said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to formally accuse someone in court.

clue.text: Sort of paint responsible for beastly illness

definitions.meaning: a water-based paint for walls and ceilings
a viral disease of dogs and other animals

explanation.surface: A paint is blamed for making animals sick.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a glue-bound wall paint and a contagious viral disease of dogs.

clue.text: Maintain silence about a learned person's ruin

indicators.note: about says the call for quiet goes around the graduate

parts.note: ssh is the call for quiet
an MA, Master of Arts, is a learned graduate

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about a scholar's downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: To smash something is to wreck or destroy it.

clue.text: A bird found in most regrettable condition

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird is discovered in a very sorry state.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a white heron with long plumes.

clue.text: Drier that might be of poor quality

indicators.note: might be says the letters of the words drier that could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A tumble-drier that could be shoddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something low-grade is inferior, ranked well below the best.

clue.text: Initiated new provisional authority?

indicators.note: new says the letters of the word initiated are made into a new word

explanation.surface: A temporary government has just been inaugurated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provisional authority' reads as a caretaker government; it means an expert on provisions, that is food.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrition expert is an authority on diet and food supplies.

clue.text: The sweet-brier for instance can line the track

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for instance

indicators.note: to line something is to be inside it, so the can goes within the track

parts.note: a lane is a narrow track or road
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A wild rose, for example, might grow along a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' looks like 'stand along' but works as a container: the can lines the inside of the track.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is another name for the sweet-brier, a wild rose with fragrant leaves.

clue.text: Release or face imprisoning skinhead girl

indicators.note: imprisoning says the clock face holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch
the head, or first letter, of the word skin
miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Someone must free or confront a jailed skinhead girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' reads as a shaven-headed youth but means the head of 'skin', its first letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismissal is the act of letting someone go, sending them away or discharging them.

clue.text: One's not allowed to stay after a large number protest

indicators.note: after says the rest comes behind the large number

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
one's is read as one is, the word for one spelt out being dropped to leave just the verb
someone sent away or sent off is not allowed to stay

explanation.surface: A person told to leave protests after a big crowd gathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as 'one is', so IS; D is Roman 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent is disagreement voiced against an official view.

clue.text: Urge turning in a celebrity causing shock

indicators.note: in says the reversed word goes inside the celebrity

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: turning says the word for urge is read backwards

parts.note: to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: A famous person's change of heart causes shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' is the reversal signal and 'in' the container; 'Urge' hides as a noun but is the verb as in 'egg on'. 'causing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish or astound them.

clue.text: Jack's a scoundrel!

definitions.meaning: the jack is the court card below the queen

explanation.surface: Jack is a villain!
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the jack in a pack of cards and a dishonest rogue.

clue.text: At fifty a harbour worker for Georgian capital

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'At fifty a harbour worker for Georgian capital' (7): AT + L + ANT + A gives the answer, but 'harbour' has no job and the A comes before the worker in the clue, so no honest parse fits as held.
annotationWithheld.clue: At fifty a harbour worker for Georgian capital

clue.text: Tried writing a newspaper leader?

parts.note: an essay is a piece of writing
the ed, editor, leads a newspaper

explanation.surface: An attempt at a newspaper's editorial column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' suggests an editorial article, but it is the person in charge, the editor, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to attempt it.

clue.text: The way to offer support must be settled

parts.note: St, street, is a way or road
aid is help or support

explanation.surface: A method of giving help must be fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid means sedate and fixed in one's ways, steady and unadventurous.

clue.text: Rely on a superb car when there's lots of cash available

definitions.note: plural noun, matching rolls of money

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a Rolls, a Rolls-Royce, is a luxury car

explanation.surface: Count on a luxury car when there is plenty of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A bankroll is a supply of money, a wad of notes held ready to spend.

clue.text: The French gaining entry to a club act sheepishly

indicators.note: gaining entry to says the French word goes inside the club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French people barge into a club and behave awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheepishly' reads as embarrassed, but it means like a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep make a bleating cry, so to act like a sheep is to give that call.

clue.text: Weapon of the left in general

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the word for general

parts.note: rife means widespread or general
L abbreviates left

explanation.surface: A weapon used by the political left as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-barrelled firearm with a grooved bore is a gun.

clue.text: Impress certain points on serious follower

indicators.note: follower says the word for serious comes after the points

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass points
grave means solemn or serious

explanation.surface: Make a lasting impression on a solemn disciple.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is to cut or imprint marks into a surface, or fix firmly in the mind.

clue.text: Early life as visualised

definitions.meaning: babyhood, the first years of life
split as two words it means in the imagination, as pictured in the mind

explanation.surface: Childhood as one pictures it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means babyhood, and split as in fancy it means imagined.

clue.text: It's wrong taking in people suffering

indicators.note: taking in says the legal wrong surrounds the people

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are people

explanation.surface: It is unjust to take in people who are in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: A TORT is a legal term for a civil wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe mental or physical anguish.

clue.text: Mere lad in revolt — so green

indicators.note: in revolt suggests overturning, so the letters of the words mere lad are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mere boy rebels, so he is inexperienced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like 'naive' to suit the lad, but it means the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald is a bright green shade, named after the gemstone.
